conviction_note: Sized jointly, not additively: a 53.76m-ADS unregistered block (9.2% of the 585.8m float) came free of lock-up on 2026-08-23 in the middle of the +68% run-up, and the only mechanism that would absorb it -- the US$30m buyback re-announced on 2026-08-04 -- has a documented 6.7% utilisation rate that the Sept 8 release must disclose; against that I hold back for a 9.13% short base with 6.0 days to cover and a BTC treasury now ~$44m above its stale 30-Jun mark, either of which can squeeze this the other way, so -4.0% rather than the double-digit number 183% realised vol would permit.

findings.finding: Cipher Mining's 53,762,660 CAN ADSs (806,439,900 Class A shares, ~9.2% of the 585.8m reported float), issued to it at US$0.7394/ADS on 2026-02-23 as payment for the ABC Projects JV stake, came out of lock-up on 2026-08-23 -- Cipher's own 10-Q states the date and carries the position inside 'Prepaid expenses and other current assets', and the shares were never registered for resale, so Cipher can sell under Rule 144 as a non-affiliate with no volume cap and no Form 144 trail.
findings.why_not_priced: The block is invisible to every screen that quotes this name: stockanalysis.com's float of 585.80m excludes it, Canaan's own EDGAR filer index shows no Schedule 13G or 13D from Cipher (CIK 1819989) among the 13Gs on file, Canaan filed no resale registration for it (the 2026-05-22 POS AM to F-3 333-285125 is a $270m primary shelf and names no selling shareholder), and Cipher as a non-affiliate owes no Form 144. If the market had focused on it, CAN would not have risen 68% in 20 days straight through the expiry date with a 9%-of-float unregistered block coming loose, and the 25-delta skew would exist at all rather than the chain being one-sided and untradeable. Instead the tape only began to show it three sessions before the print: CAN closed 2026-09-04 down 8.47% on a day bitcoin rose 2.26% to $79,697. Cipher has already written the stake down from $39.75m (a $16.5m fair-value loss booked in Q1 alone), is funding an AI/HPC datacentre conversion at the same Black Pearl site whose rigs it sold, and has classified the holding as a current asset -- three reasons it monetises into the highest-volume session this stock will see, which is the print.
findings.independence: Two independent supports. (1) Canaan's own 2026-02-23 press release states the 806,439,900 shares / 53,762,660 ADS, the US$0.7394 price and the six-month lock-up: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/canaan-inc-acquires-cipher-minings-interest-in-multiple-operational-mining-projects-totaling-4-4-ehs-in-west-texas-302694773.html (2026-02-23). (2) The share-count arithmetic corroborates the block is still outstanding and unabsorbed: Class A went from 10,431,482,973 at 2025-12-31 (20-F cover, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926043786/can-20251231x20f.htm, filed 2026-04-15) to 11,237,922,873 at 2026-05-22 (quoted from Canaan's POS AM by Weiss Asset Management's 13G/A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000135755026000026/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml, 2026-08-11) -- a difference of exactly 806,439,900, the Cipher shares and nothing else. The 2026-09-04 price/volume divergence is from a different source again: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/can/statistics/ (read 2026-09-07).

findings.finding: The 2026-08-04 'repurchase shares using digital asset treasury' release that lit the +68% run adds no new authorisation and no dollar figure -- it points back to a US$30m board authorisation dated 2025-12-12 that expires 2026-12-12 and that Canaan's own Q1 release says had bought only ~2.8m ADSs for ~US$2.0m (6.7%), after the prior US$30m programme executed just US$4.9m (16%); the Sept 8 release is the first document that must state repurchases through 30 June.
findings.why_not_priced: The wire treated it as a new programme -- headlines read 'Canaan authorizes crypto sales to fund $30 million share repurchase program' -- and the stock rose 12.43% that session and has not given the gain back. If the market had checked utilisation it would have priced an option worth ~$28m of residual capacity on a company that has used 16% and then 6.7% of two consecutive identical authorisations while its Class A count rose 806m shares, i.e. net issuer not net repurchaser over the exact life of the 'buyback'. The specific unpriced item is a number that does not yet exist in public: repurchases between 2026-04-01 and 2026-06-30, when the ADS traded $0.15-$0.43 and the company held $43.5m of cash against a negative 36.5% gross margin. A near-zero figure removes the bid that the run-up assumed.
findings.independence: Partly dependent on finding 1 and deliberately sized small for that reason -- the buyback is the only mechanism that would absorb the Cipher block, so the two are the same float question read from opposite ends and must not be added. Independent documents: the authorisation size and 12-month term, and the 16% execution of the predecessor programme, come from Canaan's 2025-12 renewal release (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/canaan-inc-renews-its-us30-million-share-buyback-program-302644432.html); the 2.8m ADS / US$2.0m utilisation, the 690,594,191 ADS count, the $43.5m cash and the US$35-45m Q2 guide come from the Q1 release (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/canaan-inc-reports-unaudited-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-302776028.html, 2026-05-19).

searched_and_found_nothing: ATM / shelf dilution, the sweep's primary hypothesis: it is NOT happening. Class A rose from 10,431,482,973 (2025-12-31, 20-F cover) to 11,237,922,873 (2026-05-22, POS AM No.4 to F-3 333-285125), a difference of exactly the 806,439,900 Cipher shares, so zero ATM issuance in five months; the $270m shelf sits unused and stockanalysis.com's 744.84m share count is consistent with no issuance since May. This is a mildly positive absence and I am reporting it rather than inventing a dilution finding.
No 424B5 anywhere in Canaan's 2026 filing history (EDGAR submissions API, CIK 0001780652, read 2026-09-07) -- no registered-direct or takedown to find.

A '160-for-1 share consolidation' EGM dated 2026-09-03 surfaced repeatedly in search and is NOT Canaan: the notice states par value US$0.0001 and 3,000,000,000 authorised shares, whereas Canaan's par is US$0.00000005 with 11.2bn Class A outstanding, and Canaan has filed no 6-K of any kind since 2026-08-17. Discarded as a relabelled other-issuer document.

A Citibank 'NOTICE OF ADS RATIO CHANGE / REVERSE SPLIT' returned as a top hit for Canaan (https://depositaryreceipts.citi.com/adr/common/file.aspx?idf=7873) is NIP Group Inc., dated 2026-06-15. Discarded.

Nasdaq minimum bid: real but wire copy. Second 180-day period runs to 2027-01-11 (Canaan 6-K exhibit 2026-07-15) and the release says only that the company 'will evaluate all available options' -- no reverse-split or ADS-ratio commitment, no EGM noticed, and an ADS ratio change needs no shareholder vote, so it can appear at ~3 weeks' notice any time before ~mid-December. Nothing dates it to 2026-09-08 and I would not sign a number to it.
Q2 revenue itself: guidance US$35-45m, and the one recent test of Canaan's guidance was clean (Q1 2026 guided $60-70m, delivered $62.7m). No edge in the top line.

The Q2 bitcoin fair-value mark is knowable and stale, not unpriced: BTC $66,710 at 2026-03-31 and $58,504 at 2026-06-30 (Fortune daily quotes, /price-of-bitcoin-03-31-2026/ and /price-of-bitcoin-06-30-2026/) imply roughly -$17m of mark on 1,807.6 BTC / 3,951.5 ETH, while BTC at $79,697 on 2026-09-04 puts the treasury ~$44m above the 30-June mark. The +68.2% 20-day run-up IS that mark-up. Priced.

Monthly self-mining production fell 90 / 90 / 64 / 46 BTC across April-July 2026 even as month-end total operating hashrate hit a 2026 high of 14.24 EH/s in July -- a genuine anomaly (month-end snapshots clearly do not describe the month), but it is published in press releases the market saw on 2026-08-17 and rose afterwards, the segment is only ~$3.7m/month of revenue at current BTC, and the honest reading is ambiguous for direction because a late-July fleet restart implies August production jumps. No signed number taken.
Ethiopia (4.96 EH/s, 157.5 MW non-North-America) power curtailment risk: nothing dated and specific found.
Bitcoin Asia 2026 (Hong Kong, 27-28 August): Canaan showed three consumer miners (Avalon Nano 3S, Avalon Mini 3, AvalonQ). Booth-level product news with no order or revenue disclosure attached.

Insider trail: CEO Zhang and CFO Cheng bought 1,065,000 ADSs at $0.35 in June 2026 (Forms 4 of 2026-06-18 and 2026-06-22, 6-K of 2026-06-24). Already disclosed and the stock fell 5.87% that day. No Form 4 cluster since.
Liquidity/going-concern angle deflated by the company's own disclosure that it collected ~US$42m of customer receivables in April 2026, on top of $43.5m cash at 31 March.
No usable option chain (baseline: ATM legs not two-sided), so there is no implied move or skew to test a finding against, and I have not substituted one.
baseline_tension: Both findings cut directly against the +68.2% 20-day run-up rather than agreeing with it, and they are not a 'the stock is cheap' argument on a beaten-down name -- they are the argument that the specific thing that drove the run (an $30m treasury-funded buyback bid) is 93% unexercised while a 9%-of-float unregistered block became sellable on 23 August; there is no skew to agree or disagree with because the chain is one-sided, and the honest counterweight is that 9.13% short interest at 6.0 days to cover plus a treasury now ~$44m above its stale 30-June mark makes the upside tail on this print fatter than my -4.0% point estimate suggests.
